'''Madhav Dhananjaya Gadgil''' (24 May 1942 – 7 January 2026) was an Indian ecologist,<ref name=Telegraph>{{cite web |last=Gadgil |first=Madhav |title=My Fundays |url=http://www.telegraphindia.com/1060223/asp/telekids/story_5886178.asp |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120911164553/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1060223/asp/telekids/story_5886178.asp |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 September 2012 |publisher=The telegraph |access-date=11 January 2012}}</ref> academic, writer, columnist and the founder of the Centre for Ecological Sciences,<ref name="Centre for Ecological Sciences">{{cite web |url=http://ces.iisc.ernet.in/new/ |title=Centre for Ecological Sciences |publisher=Indian Institute of Science |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> a research unit of the [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="HONORARY MEMBERSHIP AWARD">{{cite web |url=http://www.esa.org/history/Awards/bulletin/honorary2001.pdf |title=HONORARY MEMBERSHIP AWARD |publisher=Ecological Society of America |date=2015 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref> He was a member of the Scientific Advisory Council to the [[Prime Minister of India]] and the Head of the [[Western Ghats]] Ecology Expert Panel (WGEEP) of 2010, popularly known as the [[Gadgil Commission]].<ref name="FDI does not benefit any country">{{cite web |url=http://www.rediff.com/business/slide-show/slide-show-1-inter-fdi-does-not-benefit-any-country-madhav-gadgil/20120727.htm |title=FDI does not benefit any country |publisher=ReDiff Business |date=27 July 2012 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref><ref name="Report of the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel">{{cite web |url=http://moef.nic.in/downloads/public-information/wg-23052012.pdf |title=Report of the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel |publisher=Ministry of Environment and Forests |date=2015 |access-date=7 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920103920/http://www.moef.nic.in/downloads/public-information/wg-23052012.pdf |archive-date=20 September 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Gadgil was a recipient of the [[Volvo Environment Prize]] and the [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite Q|Q140255010}}</ref> The [[Government of India]] awarded him the fourth highest civilian award of the [[Padma Shri]] in 1981 and followed it up with the third highest award of the [[Padma Bhushan]] in 2006.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web |url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |title=Padma Awards |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India |date=2015 |access-date=21 July 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=15 October 2015}}</ref> He received the [[Champions of the Earth]] in 2024.<ref name="Ecologist Madhav Gadgil gets U.N.'s highest environmental honour, says he 'stood up for what's right'">{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=2024-12-10 |title=Ecologist Madhav Gadgil gets U.N.'s highest environmental honour, says he 'stood up for what's right' |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/energy-and-environment/ecologist-madhav-gadgil-gets-uns-highest-environmental-honour-says-he-stood-up-for-whats-right/article68969474.ece |access-date=2024-12-12 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Early life and academic career ==
Gadgil was born on 24 May 1942<ref name="Madhav Gadgil was a nation builder: Jairam Ramesh">{{Cite web |title=Madhav Gadgil was a nation builder: Jairam Ramesh |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/madhav-gadgil-a-nation-builder-his-influence-on-public-policy-was-profound-jairam-ramesh-3855077 |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref><ref name="IAS Fellow">{{cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/php/fell_all.php3?alpha=G |title=IAS Fellow |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> in [[Pune]], in the western Indian state of [[Maharashtra]]. His parents were Pramila and [[Dhananjay Ramchandra Gadgil]], a Cambridge scholar,<ref name="In love with life">{{cite journal |title=In love with life |author=Gadgil, M. |journal=Seminar |date=September 1993 |issue=409 |pages=25–30}}</ref> economist, former director of the [[Gokhale Institute]] and the author of the [[Gadgil formula]].<ref name="Shri. Dhananjayrao Gadgil">{{cite web |url=http://sahakarbharati.jagojantajago.org/DhananjayraoGadgil.aspx |title=Shri. Dhananjayrao Gadgil |publisher=Saharakar Bharati |date=2015 |access-date=10 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000856/http://sahakarbharati.jagojantajago.org/DhananjayraoGadgil.aspx |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He graduated in biology from [[Fergusson College]] of the [[University of Pune]] in 1963, and secured a master's degree in zoology from the [[Mumbai University]] in 1965.<ref name="INSA Fellow">{{cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N84-0244 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812222801/http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N84-0244 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=12 August 2016 |title=INSA Fellow |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |date=2015 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref><ref name="How Much Should a Person Consume?: Environmentalism in India and the United States">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fQxSxT_yWwYC&q=%22In+love+with+life%22+Seminar+gadgil&pg=PA192 |title=How Much Should a Person Consume?: Environmentalism in India and the United States |publisher=University of California Press |author=Ramachandra Guha |year=2006 |pages=262 |isbn=9780520248038}}</ref>

=== Harvard years ===
Gadgil was encouraged to join [[Harvard University]] by Giles Mead, then curator of fishes at the [[Harvard Museum of Comparative Zoology]]. Initially intending to do research under Mead, Gadgil later changed subjects by hearing lectures of [[E. O. Wilson]], "the brightest young star in the ecology-evolution end of biology at Harvard at that time," and subsequently did his doctoral research on mathematical ecology and fish behaviour, under the guidance of William Bossert,<ref name="In love with life" /><ref name=":0" /> one of Wilson's former students.<ref name="Wilson">{{harv|Michael L. Lewis|2003|pp=109–137}}</ref>

It earned him a PhD in 1969.<ref name="2015 Tyler Laureates">{{cite web |url=http://tylerprize.usc.edu/laureates.html |title=2015 Tyler Laureates |publisher=University of Southern California |date=2015 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref> Subsequently, he received a Fellowship from [[IBM]] to continue his work as a research fellow at the Harvard Computing Center and simultaneously worked as a lecturer of biology at the university for two years.<ref name="2015 Tyler Laureates" />

=== Return to India ===
Gadgil returned to India in 1971<ref name="My tryst with the monsoon">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/public/Resources/Initiatives/Women_in_Science/Contributors/sulochana.pdf |title=My tryst with the monsoon |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |date=2015 |access-date=11 March 2021 |author=Sulochana Gadgil}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> and took up a job as a scientific officer at [[Agharkar Research Institute]] of the Maharashtra Association for Cultivation of Science, Pune where he stayed for two years.<ref name="INSA Fellow" /> In 1973, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc), [[Bengaluru]], starting an association that would stretch for over thirty years, superannuating from the institute as its chairman in 2004.<ref name="INSA Fellow" /> During this period, he established two research centres at IISc, the ''Centre of Theoretical Studies'' and the ''Centre for Ecological Studies''.<ref name="2015 Tyler Laureates" /> He also worked as a visiting professor at [[Stanford University]] (1991) and the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1995). After his retirement from IISc, he went back to Pune in 2004 to resume his association with Agharkar Research Institute<ref name="INSA Fellow" /> and held the [[Damodar Dharmanand Kosambi]] chair of the visiting research professor at the [[University of Goa]].<ref name="Visiting Research Professor">{{cite web |url=https://www.unigoa.ac.in/vrpp/gadgil |title=Visiting Research Professor |publisher=University of Goa |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref><ref name="Madhav Gadgil to file Goa's ecological history">{{cite web |url=http://article.wn.com/view/2013/06/16/Madhav_Gadgil_to_file_Goas_ecological_history/ |title=Madhav Gadgil to file Goa's ecological history |publisher=VN |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref>

In 1976, when the [[Government of Karnataka]] decided to look into protecting the bamboo resources of the state, Gadgil was asked to conduct a study, which is reported to have influenced the government to curb the subsidies provided to forest-based industries.<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile">{{cite web |url=http://www.iiap.res.in/MadhavGadgil |title=Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile |publisher=Indian Institute of Astrophysics |date=2015 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref> A decade later, in 1986, he was appointed a member of the Scientific Advisory Council to Prime Minister of India, a post he held till 1990.<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /> During this period, he assisted the efforts to establish the first [[biosphere]] reserve in the country at the [[Nilgiris]] in 1986.<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /> In 1998, he was appointed the chairman of the ''Science and Technology Advisory Panel of Global Environment Facility'', an agency under the United Nations. He held the chair till 2002. He also served as a member of the environmental education panel of the [[National Council of Educational Research and Training]] (NCERT) and as a member of the [[National Advisory Council]].<ref name="Why India must protect the Western Ghats from getting lost">{{cite web |url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/india/why-india-must-protect-the-western-ghats-from-getting-lost/story-gvb5C0b1PJAZlw211YUxOM.html |title=Why India must protect the Western Ghats from getting lost |publisher=Hindustan Times |date=2 February 2014 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref> He was a member of the [[National Tiger Conservation Authority]]<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /> and was the chairman of the committee proposing ''Environmental Education Curriculum'' at School level.<ref name="User profile">{{cite web |url=http://www.eoearth.org/profile/Madhav.gadgil |title=User profile |publisher=Encyclopedia of Earth |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> In 2010, when the Government of India constituted an expert panel, ''Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel'' (WGEEP), to examine the ecological issues related to the [[Western Ghats]], he was selected as the chairman of the panel.<ref name="Gadgil committee recommendations on Western Ghats ideal, practical: Experts">{{cite web |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/home/environment/developmental-issues/Gadgil-committee-recommendations-on-Western-Ghats-ideal-practical-Experts/articleshow/41136674.cms |title=Gadgil committee recommendations on Western Ghats ideal, practical: Experts |publisher=Times of India |date=29 August 2014 |access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Personal life and death ==
Gadgil, an active sportsman during his college years, held the Maharashtra State Junior and [[Pune University]] high jump records in 1959 and 1961 respectively. He has also represented Pune University at the All India University Athletic meet.<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile">{{cite web |url=http://www.nieindia.org/wp-content/uploads/FellowsCV/Gadgil_M/M_Gadgil.pdf |title=National Institute of Engineering profile |publisher=National Institute of Engineering |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> He was married to [[Sulochana Gadgil]], a [[meteorologist]] and a [[Harvard University|Harvard]] scholar, whom he met during his Fergusson College years.<ref name="My tryst with the monsoon" /> The couple has a daughter, who is a journalist cum Spanish teacher, and a son who is a mathematician.<ref name="How Much Should a Person Consume?: Environmentalism in India and the United States" /><ref name="My tryst with the monsoon" /> The family lives in Pune, his home town. His life story has been recorded in a biographical book, ''Vidnyanyatri – Dr. Madhav Gadgil'', written in [[Marathi language|Marathi]] by A. P. Deshpande.<ref name="Vidnyanyatri - Dr. Madhav Gadgil">{{cite book |url=http://www.menakabooks.com/rajhans-prakashan/5152-vidnyanyatri-dr-madhav-gadgil-a-p-deshapnde-rajhans-prakashan-buy-online.html?nosto=nosto-page-category1 |title=Vidnyanyatri – Dr. Madhav Gadgil |publisher=Rajhans Prakashan |author=A. P. Deshpande |date=2011 |isbn=9788174345516 |access-date=8 October 2015 |archive-date=29 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629112035/http://www.menakabooks.com/rajhans-prakashan/5152-vidnyanyatri-dr-madhav-gadgil-a-p-deshapnde-rajhans-prakashan-buy-online.html?nosto=nosto-page-category1 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Gadgil died in [[Pune]] on 7 January 2026, at the age of 83.<ref name="Renowned ecologist Madhav Gadgil passes away at 82">{{Cite news |date=January 8, 2026 |title=Renowned ecologist Madhav Gadgil passes away at 82 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/renowned-ecologist-madhav-gadgil-passes-away-at-82/article70485030.ece |access-date=2026-01-08 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.lokmat.com/pune/senior-environmental-expert-madhav-gadgil-passes-away-a-a653/|title= ज्येष्ठ पर्यावरण तज्ज्ञ माधव गाडगीळ यांचे निधन, वयाच्या ८३ व्या वर्षी घेतला अखेरचा श्वास | work= [[Lokmat]]|date=8 January 2026|access-date=8 January 2026}}</ref> He was survived by his son and daughter, and was predeceased by his wife, who died in July 2025.<ref name="Veteran ecologist, Madhav Gadgil, passes away in Pune after brief illness">{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2026 |title=Veteran ecologist, Madhav Gadgil, passes away in Pune after brief illness |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/veteran-ecologist-madhav-gadgil-passes-in-pune-after-brief-illness-101767833929633.html |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
[[File:Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve.jpg|thumb|left|220px|[[Nilgiris]] Biosphere Reserve]]
[[File:Poomparai village.jpg|thumb|240px|[[Poombarai]] village in the [[Western Ghats]].]]
One of the major contributions of Gadgil is his effort towards the preservation of ecology of India. His early researches in the 1980s have helped in the identification of the [[Nilgiris]] as the first [[biosphere]] reserve in India.<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /> As the chairman of the ''Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel'' (WGEEP), which later came to be known as the [[Gadgil Commission]], he submitted a report in 2011,<ref name="Vested interests harm Western Ghats">{{cite web |url=http://www.deccanherald.com/content/395071/vested-interests-harm-western-ghats.html |title=Vested interests harm Western Ghats |publisher=Deccan Herald |date=28 March 2014 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> marking around 64 percent of the Western Ghats region as ''Ecologically Sensitive Area'' (ESA).<ref name="Why India must protect the Western Ghats from getting lost" /> The report attracted support and dissension,<ref name="Tyler Prize">{{cite web |url=http://tylerprize.usc.edu/laureates.html#gadgil |title=Tyler Prize |publisher=University of Southern California |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> the environmentalists welcoming the recommendations and the state governments of the neighbouring states and the [[Syro-Malabar Catholic Church]] of Kerala disapproving it.<ref name="Gadgil committee recommendations on Western Ghats ideal, practical: Experts" /><ref name="Vested interests harm Western Ghats" /> This paved way for the subsequent [[Gadgil Committee#Kasturirangan Report|Kasturirangan Commission]], which diluted the recommendations to a level more acceptable to the state governments.<ref name="Why India must protect the Western Ghats from getting lost" /> He has been credited by many with the introduction of quantitative investigations of ecology and animal behaviour in India and for including humans as a vital part of [[ecosystems]].<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /><ref name="Central University of Orissa DSc">{{cite web |url=http://eodishasamachar.com/en/central-university-of-orissa-confers-degree-of-doctor-of-science-honoris-causa-to-professor-madhav-gadgil/ |title=Central University of Orissa DSc |publisher=Odisha Samachar |work=2013 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> His contributions, as a member of the draft committee, has been reported in the preparation of the Biological Diversity Act 2002<ref name="People’s Biodiversity Registers">{{cite web |url=http://ces.iisc.ernet.in/PBR.html |title=People's Biodiversity Registers |publisher=Centre for Ecological Sciences |date=2006 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> and the manual he prepared for the ''People's Biodiversity Registers'' has been accepted by the [[National Biodiversity Authority]].<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile" /> He was still associated with the Authority in the preparation of a biodiversity inventory at the local bodies' level.<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile" />

Gadgil is known to have done extensive researches in the areas of [[population biology]], [[conservation biology]], [[human ecology]] and [[History of ecology|ecological history]]. His researches have been documented by over 250 scientific articles,<ref name="INSA Fellow" /> published in various journals and magazines.<ref name="IAS Open Access Repository">{{cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Gadgil=3AMadhav_Dhananjaya=3A=3A.html |title=IAS Open Access Repository |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> He developed a penchant for writing at an early age and his first publication was a series of ten articles on animal behaviour, published in ''[[Srishtidnyan]]'', a [[Marathi language]] science magazine, when he was studying in the 10th standard.<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /> His doctoral thesis is reported to have been a citation classic.<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics profile" /><ref name="National Institute of Ecology profile">{{cite web |url=http://www.nieindia.org/wp-content/uploads/FellowsCV/Gadgil_M/CV-MADHAV-GADGIL.doc |title=National Institute of Ecology profile |publisher=National Institute of Ecology |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015 |archive-date=6 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306044323/http://www.nieindia.org/wp-content/uploads/FellowsCV/Gadgil_M/CV-MADHAV-GADGIL.doc |url-status=dead }}</ref> He published his first book in English, ''[[This Fissured Land]]'', a book on the ecological history of India, in 1992.<ref name="This Fissured Land">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=D9iwuQAACAAJ |title=This Fissured Land |publisher=Oxford University Press India |author=Madhav Gadgil, Ramachandra Guha |year=1992 |pages=312 |isbn=9780198077442}}</ref> The next book, ''Ecology and Equity: The Use and Abuse of Nature in Contemporary India'',<ref name="Ecology and Equity: The Use and Abuse of Nature in Contemporary India">{{cite book |title=Ecology and Equity: The Use and Abuse of Nature in Contemporary India |publisher=Routeledge |author=Madhav Gadgil, Ramachandra Guha |year=1995 |pages=223 |isbn=978-0415125246}}</ref> again co-authored by [[Ramachandra Guha]], was released in 1995, followed by ''Nurturing Biodiversity: An Indian Agenda'', a book co-authored by P. R. Seshagiri Rao, in 1998.<ref name="Nurturing Biodiversity: An Indian Agenda">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gt_aAAAAMAAJ |title=Nurturing Biodiversity: An Indian Agenda |publisher=Centre for Environment Education |author=Madhav Gadgil, P. R. Seshagiri Rao |year=1998 |pages=163 |isbn=9788186385135}}</ref> In 2005, he published two books, ''Diversity : The cornerstone of life''<ref name="Diversity : The cornerstone of life">{{cite book |url=http://www.bookswala.in/Science-Fiction/Diversity-The-Cornerstone-Of-Life-BW-726?limit=75 |title=Diversity : The cornerstone of life |publisher=Vigyan Prasar |author=Madhav Gadgil |year=2005 |pages=64 |isbn=8174800263}}</ref> and ''Ecological Journeys''.<ref name="Ecological Journeys">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8XJ2HHZcM6oC |title=Ecological Journeys |publisher=Orient Blackswan |author=Madhav Gadgil |year=2005 |pages=257 |isbn=9788178241128}}</ref> As a part of his responsibilities as a ''Pew Fellow in Conservation and the Environment'',<ref name="PEW Fellow">{{cite web |url=http://www.pewtrusts.org/sitecore/content/pewtrusts_org/projects/marine-fellows/fellows-directory/1993/madhav-gadgil?sc_lang=en |title=PEW Fellow |publisher=The PEW Charitable Trusts |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> he has contributed towards the preparation of ''People's Biodiversity Registers'' and has published a manual, ''People's Biodiversity Registers: A Methodology Manual''.<ref name="KVIFF Honours">{{cite web |url=http://www.kirloskarvasundharafest.in/kviff-madhav-gadgil.html |title=KVIFF Honours |publisher=Kirloskar Vasundhara |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}{{Dead link|date=March 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="Ecology is for the People:  A Methodology Manual for People’s  Biodiversity Register">{{cite web |url=http://nbaindia.in/uploaded/docs/ec_for_ppl.pdf |title=Ecology is for the People: A Methodology Manual for People's Biodiversity Register |publisher=Centre for Ecological Sciences |date=2006 |access-date=8 October 2015 |author=Madhav Gadgil |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304074318/http://nbaindia.in/uploaded/docs/ec_for_ppl.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Some of his books have been translated into many languages and serve as texts for academic studies.<ref name="Tyler Prize" /> He has also published two books,<ref name="Visiting Research Professor" /> ''Nisarganiyojan Lokasahabhagane'' being one among them,<ref name="National Institute of Ecology profile" /> and over 40 articles in Marathi and handled a fortnightly column on natural history, in [[The Hindu]], from 1999 till 2004.<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile" /> He handled a monthly column in the Marathi daily, [[Sakal]].<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile" />

== Awards and recognition ==
[[File:Dr. Madhav Gadgil and Col. Ashwin Baindur at Wikidata workshop in Pune on 18 September 2017.jpg|thumb|Dr. Madhav Gadgil (right) and Col. Ashwin Baindur (left, in white shirt) at a Wikidata workshop in Pune on 18 September 2017]]
The [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA) elected him as their Fellow in 1984.<ref name="INSA Fellow" /> Six years later, the two other major science academies of India, The [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (IAS)<ref name="IAS Fellow" /> and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] (NASI), followed suit by electing him as a Fellow in 1990.<ref name="NASI Fellow">{{cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=G |title=NASI Fellow |publisher=National Academy of Sciences India |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021102942/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=G |archive-date=21 October 2014}}</ref> He was Fellow of the [[Third World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS), an honorary Fellow of the Association for Tropical Biology and Conservation (ATBC) and a recipient of the National Environment Fellowship of the [[Ministry of Environment and Forests]] for his field research in the [[Western Ghats]].<ref name="Honorary Fellow ATBC">{{cite web |url=http://tropicalbiology.org/honorary-fellow-atbc-2010-dr-madhav-gadgil/ |title=Honorary Fellow ATBC |publisher=Association for Tropical Biology and Conservation |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> He was elected as a Foreign Associate of the [[US National Academy of Sciences]] in 1991<ref name="Foreign Associate">{{cite web |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/madhav-gadgil-j9pywz/ |title=Foreign Associate |publisher=[U.S. National Academy of Sciences |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> and he served as a member of the [[British Ecological Society]] and Ecological Society of America.<ref name="HONORARY MEMBERSHIP AWARD" /><ref name="Honorary Fellow ATBC" />

The Government of India awarded him the fourth highest civilian honour of the [[Padma Shri]] in 1981<ref name="Padma Awards" /> and the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR), an autonomous government agency awarded him [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], the highest Indian award in the Science and Technology sector, in 1986.<ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize">{{cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Prize_Winner_Index%20(Alphabetical).htm |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> In between, in 1983, the Government of Karnataka honoured him with [[Rajyotsava Prashasthi]], their second highest civilian award.<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile" /> His alma mater, [[Harvard University]], presented him with the [[Harvard Centennial Medal]], an annual honour given to its alumni for their achievements in their respective field of service, in 2002.<ref name="Harvard Centennial Medal">{{cite web |url=http://www.gsas.harvard.edu/alumni/gsas_centennial_medalists.php |title=Harvard Centennial Medal |publisher=Harvard University |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The next year, he shared the 2003 [[Volvo Environment Prize]] of the Volvo Environment Prize Foundation, with [[Muhammad Yunus]], the [[social entrepreneur]] from Bangladesh.<ref name="Volvo Environment Prize">{{cite web |url=http://www.environment-prize.com/laureates/by-year/2003/madhav-gadgil-,-mohammad-yunus/ |title=Volvo Environment Prize |publisher=The Volvo Environment Prize Foundation |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref>

Gadgil received the [[Padma Bhushan]], the third highest civilian award from the Government of India in 2006<ref name="Padma Awards" /> and the [[H K Firodia awards|H. K. Firodia award]] of the H. K. Firodia Foundation reached him a year later, in 2007.<ref name="H K Firodia awards">{{cite web |url=http://hkfirodiaawards.org/awards_2.html |title=H K Firodia awards |publisher=H K Firodia Foundation |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304234211/http://hkfirodiaawards.org/awards_2.html |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[Central University of Orissa, Koraput|Central University of Orissa]] honoured him with the degree of Doctor of Science (Honoris Causa) in 2013<ref name="Central University of Orissa DSc" /> and [[The Energy and Resources Institute]] (TERI) recognised the contributions of the ''Western Ghats Ecology Experts Panel'' (WGEEP) and its chairman with the Georgescu-Roegen Award in 2014.<ref name="Georgescu-Roegen Award">{{cite web |url=http://dsds.teriin.org/2014/georgescu.php |title=Georgescu-Roegen Award |publisher=The Energy and Resources Institute |date=2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> The [[University of Southern California]] awarded him the [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement|John and Alice Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]] in 2015, which he shared with [[Jane Lubchenco]], a Distinguished Professor of [[Oregon State University]],<ref name="Tyler Prize" /> making him the second Indian, after [[M. S. Swaminathan]], to receive the Prize.<ref name="Indian ecologist Madhav Gadgil, US scientist Jane Lubchenco share 2015 Tyler Prize">{{cite web |url=http://zeenews.india.com/news/eco-news/indian-ecologist-madhav-gadgil-us-scientist-jane-lubchenco-share-2015-tyler-prize_1567590.html |title=Indian ecologist Madhav Gadgil, US scientist Jane Lubchenco share 2015 Tyler Prize |publisher=Zee News |date=25 March 2015 |access-date=8 October 2015}}</ref> He is also a recipient of the [[Vikram Sarabhai]] Award and [[Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar]] Award.<ref name="National Institute of Engineering profile" />

He received the Fergusson Gaurav Puraskar 2019, for being an Outstanding Alumnus from his [[Alma Mater]], [[Fergusson College]] on 6 January 2019. The [[United Nations]] awarded him the [[Champions of the Earth]] award in 2024.<ref name="Ecologist Madhav Gadgil gets U.N.'s highest environmental honour, says he 'stood up for what's right'" />

== Eponymy ==
''[[Elaeocarpus gadgilii]]'', is a tree species described in 2021 from the Nelliampathy hills in Palakkad district of Kerala, India named in honour of him.<ref>Manoharan, M.A., Prabhukumar, K.M., Arjun, S.K., Jose, S. and Veerankutty, S., 2021. Elaeocarpus gadgilii (Elaeocarpaceae), a new species from Western Ghats (India). [https://www.mapress.com/j/pt/article/view/phytotaxa.489.1.7 Phytotaxa, 489(1), pp.87-93].</ref>
A species of frog, ''[[Micrixalus gadgili]]'', is also named after him.<ref> [http://www.recordsofzsi.com/index.php/zsoi/article/download/161667/110947?__cf_chl_tk=3sLzGnb8Jhl5VCPX0i9TuU87G5lFcUW74zcQTJJhAqs-1778836874-1.0.1.1-nPHDbEZmy4o0CR7AUuMd5d7e6Ioxrg3fqsM.CRzsviQ]</ref>
